editorial:
You meet Walter Black at his lowest point, when depression has drained the joy from his family and his toy company. Instead of a normal recovery, he starts speaking through a beaver hand puppet, and that strange choice becomes the heart of this heavy drama. His wife and sons react with confusion, hope, and anger, especially Porter, who is tired of watching his father fall apart. The movie feels intimate and uncomfortable, but it also has moments of dark humor that keep it from becoming too bleak.

Mel Gibson gives a committed performance, and Jodie Foster adds warmth as Walter’s wife. The pacing is steady rather than fast, so you should expect a slow, emotional watch instead of big thrills. It handles mental health seriously, though the puppet idea may feel odd or too much for some viewers. If you like character dramas with messy family feelings, this is worth your time. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or buy the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, Walter’s puppet persona takes over and his marriage falls apart. He tries to cut off the hand wearing the beaver, but the attempt turns into a suicide attempt in the garage. The branch breaks, he survives, and the puppet is finally gone. Walter wakes in the hospital, speaks in his own voice again, and slowly rebuilds trust with Meredith and Porter. Porter’s graduation speech shows the family beginning to heal.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven family dramas.
